content:
In the past few days, there have been two reports suggesting different ways Apple could make more money by increasing its services revenue.

In my view, it absolutely should do the first one, but not the second — and it looks like Phil Schiller may well agree with that view…

Let's start by summarising these two reports.

Home security and monitoring services

On Friday, Bloomberg revealed that Apple may be planning to launch a brand-new home security and monitoring service, designed to work alongside some of the new home hardware products we were already expecting.

Squeezing more revenue from the App Store

A second report from the same source on Sunday says the company is looking at ways to squeeze more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple should not take the latter approach

Conversely, I believe the second approach would be a very significant mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly position on iPhone app sales has come under fierce criticism from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an iPhone app, you are forced to do so through the official App Store, leaving you with no choice but to accept Apple's terms without any room to negotiate.

I understand that many people argue no one is forcing you to buy an iPhone or develop apps for it, but that is not how laissez-faire capitalism actually works in practice: even in the United States, there have been antitrust laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, restrictions are imposed on you to ensure you do not abuse that position.

Trying to extract more money from the App Store goes completely against the idea of "skating to where the puck is going," and Phil Schiller is reportedly in agreement with that view, since Bloomberg indicates this is one of the reasons he has chosen to step back from his current role.

Innovative services are the right direction

By contrast, launching innovative services that people are willing to pay for is absolutely what Apple should be doing. I can easily see the value of the company offering a home security monitoring service.

Back in 2024, I already said that launching its own smart home cameras would be one of the smartest moves the company could make. I said the same about Apple's rumoured smart doorbell. Offering optional service bundles to go with security products makes complete sense, for two reasons.

First, there are the various privacy reasons I have previously mentioned. HomeKit Secure Video has already made a significant contribution to safeguarding the privacy of security camera footage. If there is one company I would trust to perform AI analysis on security camera footage, it is Apple.

Second, Apple is of course the company best positioned to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit ecosystem. I believe there are many other areas where Apple could offer similar benefits.

For me, the key is that Apple needs to treat services with the same approach it applies to hardware. Make excellent products that people willingly and happily pay for, rather than making money in ways that annoy customers, developers and regulators alike.

What are your thoughts on this? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
